title_en: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Teaser Pretty Much Confirms Fifth Playable Faction — and the Appearance of a Would-Be Chaos God
summary_en: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.
body_en:
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.
Dawn of War 4, developed by King Art Games, launches with four playable races: the Space Marines; Orks, Necrons, and the Adeptus Mechanicus. We knew that the developer had plans to release more factions over time, as has been the case with previous entries in the real-time strategy series. But we didn’t know which would come first… until now.
Warning! Potential spoilers for Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 follow.
The teaser ends with a tease for Dawn of War 4’s first DLC faction. We see the unmistakable eyes of Vashtorr the Arkifane, alongside the narration: “And what began on Aurelia is coming to Kronus.”
That’s a clear reference to Chaos as the new faction, given Aurelia, the former homeworld and capital of the Blood Ravens Space Marine Chapter, was gobbled up by the Warp (Warhammer 40,000’s version of a hell dimension full of demons), before it was spat out and besieged by Black Legion Chaos Space Marines. So, it would make sense that Chaos Space Marines are the new faction. Will we see further corruption of the Blood Ravens play out?
But what about Vashtorr the Arkifane? Vashtorr is a sort of in-between, Chaos Undivided being who appears to have designs on becoming the fifth Chaos god. According to the lore, Vashtorr came into existence within the Warp due to our obsessive pursuit of tech innovation (feels pretty relatable right now, doesn’t it?). As such, Vashtorr acts as a sort of arms dealer to the existing Chaos factions, creating powerful daemon weapons and engines for use in war.
Ever since Vashtorr’s dramatic introduction into the Warhammer 40,000 universe with the Arks of Omen storyline a few years ago, and his uneasy alliance with Horus’ successor, Abaddon the Despoiler, fans have wondered about his masterplan. As is Games Workshop’s want, the overarching Warhammer 40,000 storyline moves slowly, so we don’t really have much to go on beyond he’s big, he’s mean, and he wants it all. Perhaps Dawn of War 4 will shed more light on his motivations?
Either way, it would be really cool if we got to actually command Vashtorr on the battlefield, although you’d expect him to be incredibly overpowered, given what we know of his power set from the lore. Dawn of War 4 is the first Warhammer 40,000 video game to feature a playable Primarch (one of the Emperor’s ultra powerful sons). Could we see Lion El'Jonson go up against Vashtorr in the DLC? That would be quite something.
It’s not long before we find out. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 launches on PC on December 3, 2026.
